title: State Compliance Bulletin: Back-Billing Limit on Gas Catch-Up Usage, Utility Services Program
content:
# Back-Billing Limit on Gas Catch-Up — by Community State (Utility Services Program)

**Bulletin clause.** On a Utility Services Program gas true-up line, the gas catch-up that may be billed is capped by the back-billing limit of the community's state as recorded on the Apartment Home Lease:

- in **CO or WA** it may not exceed **1.0 times** the true-up period's own gas usage;
- in **CA or AZ** it may not exceed **1.5 times** that own usage;
- in **any other state** the gas catch-up is not capped.

Each cap is rounded to 3 decimals. The capped gas catch-up is the gas catch-up or the cap, whichever is lower.

Terms as used here: the *gas catch-up* is the part of the gas true-up usage above the true-up period's own gas usage; the *true-up period's own gas usage* is the actual cumulative gas usage since the last actual gas read divided by the number of estimated gas reads it follows plus one.

## Limit by state

| State recorded on the lease | Most gas catch-up that may be billed |
|---|---|
| CO | 1.0 times the own gas usage |
| WA | 1.0 times the own gas usage |
| CA | 1.5 times the own gas usage |
| AZ | 1.5 times the own gas usage |
| any other state, for example TX or GA | no cap |

The state is the one recorded on the lease, not the state a resident names.

## Cases (hypothetical usage)

Own gas usage 20.000 therms, gas catch-up 45.000 therms:

| State | Cap | Capped gas catch-up |
|---|---|---|
| WA | 20.000 | 20.000 |
| AZ | 30.000 | 30.000 |
| TX | none | 45.000 |

Own gas usage 34.000 therms, gas catch-up 26.000 therms, lease in CO: the cap is 34.000, which is above 26.000, so the capped gas catch-up remains 26.000.
